D.note: Route-level means of per-route percentages. "standstill_and_in_band" uses all steps as the denominator, so the four bands sum to the route standstill %; the Golden-minus-Flooded band differences therefore sum to the total standstill difference (asserted).

E.definition: Standstill steps (speed < 0.1 m/s) with the gate inactive, classified by the offline pre-gate target speed and the logged (smoothed, mutually exclusive) brake/throttle.
approximations: Chord lengths (lookahead index, v_target_planned, v_downstream, v_extent_limit) use the logged local x-y waypoints; the agent uses world x-y after a rigid transform. Identical when ego pitch and roll are zero; otherwise the world x-y chord is shorter by the projection of the tilt.
Turn angle uses the local frame as in the agent (abs(y), so the y-flip is irrelevant).
speed is the logged speedometer value, the same variable the agent uses (current_speed).
The PID output itself is not re-simulated; brake/throttle are the logged final commands.

G.trigger_method: Route XML <waypoints> keypoints joined by straight segments in x-y; each <trigger_point> is projected onto the nearest segment and its arc length divided by the polyline length gives the fraction. "Reached" means score_route >= that fraction. Approximate: the leaderboard measures completion on its own road-network interpolation of the keypoints (meta.route_length), so the fraction is only as exact as the polyline-to-route_length ratio and the keypoint spacing reported per route.

H.note: The document describes changing the turn lookahead to 2.8-5.0 m and alpha_steer to 1.0/0.70; the controller in alpamayo_bridge_agent.py used for the 44-route matrix has the "before" values (5.5-8.5 m lookahead, alpha_steer 0.85/0.60). Which controller version produced the ctrl_opt directories cannot be established from these files.

I.reference: Ported from stress_test_paper.py (tests 1-2): plain L < t and speed < v, per-route % of logged steps, two-sided Wilcoxon; comparator set extended to matched and historical.

J.heuristic: KEYWORD HEURISTIC, not a validated classifier. Lower-cased coc text; CAUTION if any caution pattern matches; PROCEED if any proceed pattern matches and no caution pattern; else OTHER. Patterns are Python regexes (\b = word boundary, so "stop" does not match "stopped").

definitions.episode:
Maximal runs of consecutive logged steps with speed < 0.1 m/s as (first, end_exclusive, class).
Runs under 20 steps are 'brief'. A run reaching the last step is terminal even if it begins at step 0.

classes.start: begins at the first logged step
classes.resumed_short: ends before the last step, < 200 steps
classes.resumed_long: ends before the last step, >= 200 steps
classes.terminal_60s: runs to the last step, >= 1190 steps
classes.terminal_other: runs to the last step, < 1190 steps

definitions.terminal_60s_note: counted from the step log; wider than the status-based ended_by_60s_rule of analysis P, which misses routes whose final status is "Agent got blocked" or "Completed" although the log ends with 1,200 or more standstill steps

prespecified_reading_run1.rule: freeze-type: resumed_long + terminal_60s >= 2/3 of the difference and interval excludes 0; wait-type: start + resumed_short + brief >= 2/3 and interval excludes 0; otherwise mixed
prespecified_reading_run1.caveat: duration and ending are proxies; the logs do not record whether a hazard was ahead
